correctness.rationale: For every n≥3 and permutation schedule, an exact single-sweep identity Hy=Jx yields the polynomial matrix tH+J. Its determinant has exactly two nonzero permutation contributions, giving Q=(t+1)^n+t^a. The transpose presentation module is cyclic because Q(0)=Q(1)=1 makes t and t+1 units and the row relations generate all coordinates from one. Therefore minimal and characteristic polynomials coincide. The standard polynomial-gcd kernel computation proves exact counts for every m≥1, with Möbius inversion for least cycles. All 6390 checked update orders, 59700 independently computed return ranks, 5978 cyclic-vector tests, and 160 orbit censuses agreed. The proof does not rely on finite testing.

value.rationale: A natural n!-sized family of asynchronous Rule-60 dynamics is compressed exactly to n-1 explicitly represented linear similarity types, with a closed gcd law for every periodic-point count, every primitive cycle count, and the global order at all ring sizes. Non-squarefree cases are covered. On six sites even the full-sweep permutation order takes three values (14,15,21), demonstrating mathematical dynamical sensitivity to schedule. Unlike routine characteristic-polynomial calculation for one matrix, the theorem handles all permutations and proves an unrestricted cyclic-module structure. This is a structural orbit classification, not an arbitrary parameter slice.
